ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Alexander the Great

code.originalText: Nine-week review: repeat spirometry, pain, drinking and PEth, AUDIT-C, mood, safety and the plan ahead

text.paragraph: Alexander runs again and marches a full day with his kit; he is short of breath only at the top of long climbs. The scar aches at 2 of 10 after heavy training, and he uses the lidocaine patch three or four nights a week. He has kept to his drinking limits at every banquet in the past three weeks and has had no alcohol on most days. He sees the addiction medicine and behavioral health clinicians every two weeks. He sleeps six to seven hours and says the grief is still there but no longer runs his days. His HIV, hepatitis C and hepatitis B tests from the preventive visit were negative, with immunity to hepatitis B from his childhood vaccines. He is planning the next campaign. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-05-11; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 120/76, pulse 66; weight 71.5 kg
Slightly reduced breath sounds at the left base, unchanged; no crackles
Minimal tenderness over the left fifth rib; no allodynia
Bright and engaged; no thoughts of suicide

Left chest wall pain at the scar of an old penetrating arrow wound, with breathlessness on exertion and a reduced FVC (78 percent predicted) with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, and heavy episodic drinking (AUDIT 19, PEth 236 ng/mL), found at intake; cause and extent under evaluation with a pulmonology consultation and an addiction medicine assessment

S — Synthetic presenting problem anchored to the documented chest wound and the documented drinking parties; superseded at the consultation, when the chest wall pain, the pleural thickening and the alcohol use disorder were diagnosed.
Chronic post-traumatic chest wall pain: intercostal neuropathic pain at the healed left chest wound and fifth rib fracture, with tenderness and a small area of allodynia over the scar
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the consultation, anchored to the documented arrow wound; not a claim about his real chest.

Localized left pleural thickening (fibrothorax) from an old organized hemothorax after a penetrating chest wound, with a mild restrictive defect (TLC 79 percent predicted) and normal gas transfer; no retained foreign body, fistula or trapped lung on CT
S — Synthetic modern finding of the CT and lung function tests at the consultation, anchored to the documented arrow wound; the retrospective pneumothorax (CLM-0004) is not used.

Alcohol use disorder, mild (three DSM-5-TR criteria): drinking more than intended at banquets, riding after drinking, and arguments with his officers while drunk; ten or more drinks on two or three nights a week, more since his bereavement; no withdrawal; AUDIT 19; PEth 236 ng/mL

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made with the addiction medicine clinician at the consultation visit, anchored to the documented drinking parties; the criteria, amounts and scores are synthetic. The diagnosis is mild, in keeping with the disputed evidence (CLM-0008).

Bereavement five months after the death of his closest companion since boyhood, with depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 12, item 9 scored 0) that do not meet criteria for a major depressive episode; prolonged grief disorder cannot be diagnosed before twelve months
S — Synthetic modern assessment anchored to the documented bereavement; DSM-5-TR codes uncomplicated bereavement as Z63.4 whatever the relationship. Not a claim about his real mental health.
Laceration of the left forearm, 4 cm, from a practice blade in a training drill; clean edges, no tendon, nerve or vessel injury; repaired with sutures; healed
S — Synthetic acute injury; not a historical claim.

text.paragraph: Guideline basis: Standardization of Spirometry 2019 Update. An Official American Thoracic Society and European Respiratory Society Technical Statement (2019); ERS/ATS technical standard on interpretive strategies for routine lung function tests (2022); British Thoracic Society Guideline for pleural disease (2023); CDC Clinical Practice Guideline for Prescribing Opioids for Pain - United States, 2022 (2022); Unhealthy Alcohol Use in Adolescents and Adults: Screening and Behavioral Counseling Interventions (2018); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Substance Use Disorders (2021); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, depression monograph (2026); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024)

Follow-up: Primary care in three months with PEth and PHQ-9, or sooner for more breathlessness or chest pain. Pulmonology review in a year with spirometry. Addiction medicine and behavioral health every four weeks. The clinic or 988 at any hour. [S]
